reuse.why: The link-eligibility rule is one shared helper and unlink reuses the extracted clearAccountBankLink, but Fintegra linking and download copy the Akahu functions instead of sharing a common link/download path.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near line-for-line copy of linkAkahuAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions, and the same five-line assert-then-clear preamble is pasted into all six link functions.

placement.why: Link rules live in accounts/app.ts next to the link handlers, download in sync.ts beside the other providers, config and types in their usual modules.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; extracting clearAccountBankLink out of unlinkAccount is directly needed by step 4.

maintainability.why: Rules are centralised in one helper, but adding a provider still means copying a whole link and download function and remembering the preamble in each, and an 'assert' function that returns an account to unlink mixes validation with the replace decision.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every link handler, including the new Fintegra one, goes through assertCanLinkBankAccount and the shared findOrCreateBank/syncAccount/handleSyncResponse.

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions is downloadAkahuTransactions reshaped (destructured response, dropped 'error' branch and logging); the Akahu balance branch in processBankSyncDownload is widened to fintegra rather than shared by name.

abstraction_drift.where: assertCanLinkBankAccount in accounts/app.ts: step 3 adds the closed-upgrading-account branch and step 4 adds the replaceExistingLink parameter with a branch that turns the assertion into returning the account to unlink; every call site then repeats the clearAccountBankLink follow-up.
